FEEDBACK: Prevent accidental passes from missing applicability data: require exactly one constructionDate, summerLoadLineFreshWaterDraught, and upperIceWaterlineDraught, and for pre-2007 ships require the firstScheduledDryDockingDate needed to determine the deadline rather than letting its absence disable the constraint. Constrain quantity nodes and relevant booleans to single values. In the marking check, compare the mark only with the maximum amidships draught on the same qualifying classCertificate that satisfies the certificate shape; the current EXISTS may pass using a second malformed certificate or one matching value among contradictory values.

Repair applicability and the construction-date branches. Do not target every nltl:ship and thereby require every ship to have one of the six ice classes; gate all obligations to ships whose nltl:iceClass is one of the listed applicable values. The marking constraint currently ignores constructionDate and therefore imposes the immediate post-2007 rule on pre-1-July-2007 ships. Split the draught-triggered logic: for constructionDate >= 2007-07-01, require the warning triangle, ice-class draught mark, and mark draught equal to the certificate maximum amidships; for constructionDate < 2007-07-01, couple those marking obligations to the first scheduled dry-docking deadline. Do not require firstScheduledDryDockingDate merely because a ship is old when the summer-load-line/UIWL trigger is false, and do not claim the 'not later than' timing is validated unless the constraint actually represents when the deadline has been reached.

Remove the standalone constraint that requires exactly one firstScheduledDryDockingDate for every pre-1 July 2007 triggered ship; the regulation requires the marking by that event, not a dry-docking-date record, and an already correctly marked ship must not fail merely because that date is absent. Restructure the pre-2007 logic so an unmarked ship may defer the marking only when a valid first scheduled dry-docking date after 1 July 2007 is evidenced and has not yet arrived; if the marking is already complete and equals the certificate maximum amidships draught, permit conformance without dry-docking-date evidence, while ensuring missing date evidence cannot make an unmarked ship pass accidentally.
